subject: Banking
title: Student Loan Servicing Abuses
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Student Loan Servicing Abuses.

hook.text: Navient steered 60% of borrowers into forbearance instead of income-driven repayment plans.

buildup.text: Student loan servicers earn fees per account. Processing forbearance takes 2 minutes. Processing IDR takes 30 minutes.

discovery.text: Navient's practices added billions in extra interest to borrowers' balances.

twist.text: Navient settled for $1.85 billion in relief. It denied wrongdoing but agreed to cancel $1.7 billion in student loans.

climax.text: Servicers got paid for speed, not outcomes, so borrower confusion became a business model.

punchline.text: 2 minutes for the expensive option. 30 for the helpful one.

quiz.question: Why did Navient steer borrowers into forbearance?
options: Processing took 2 minutes vs 30 for cheaper repayment plans

details.summary: Student loan servicers employed by banks misapplied payments, steered borrowers away from affordable repayment plans, and charged improper fees, trapping millions in unnecessary debt and damaged credit.
details.whyItMatters: Over 43 million Americans carry student debt. When servicers prioritize their own revenue over borrower welfare, they compound a crisis that already affects housing, retirement, and economic mobility.
takeaways: Servicers steered borrowers to forbearance instead of income-based repayment
Misapplied payments caused credit damage and inflated balances
Navient paid $1.85 billion to settle servicing abuse claims

faq.question: How did loan servicers harm borrowers?
faq.answer: Servicers often pushed borrowers into forbearance, which is easier to process but accrues interest, instead of enrolling them in income-driven repayment programs that would have lowered or eliminated monthly payments.

faq.question: What happened in the Navient settlement?
faq.answer: Navient agreed to cancel $1.7 billion in subprime private student loans and pay $142 million in restitution. The settlement covered allegations that Navient steered struggling borrowers into costlier repayment options.
